reviews.comment: This class is easy as long as you do the Smartbooks for extra credit and study. Professor Faulk is a very chill professor, but he doesn't curve exams. However, a lot of the exam questions are similar to the Smartbooks, so just do them over and over again. He takes attendance for a grade on random days, so my advice would be not to skip class.

I took this class during Summer I. There were 3 proctored exams and about 7 assignments due every Tuesday, but they were all pretty easy. The simulations were the hardest part of the class, but the professor was very understanding and extended the due dates for everyone multiple times. Overall, a good class.
I recommend going to class and studying quizlet instead of paying attention to his lectures

this professor is just rude. literally ignored my email. graded by 3 exams and cartedo assignments. exams are long and boring and he throws random stuff in there that wasn't on the review. i only took him bc there was no other choice. good luck

Easy concepts with unfamiliar terminology. His lectures were a bit boring, so I skipped some, but they were helpful in explaining concepts and examples that might be on the exam. Attendance is taken once a week but you don't know when, except on guest speaker days. Review is helpful, but exhaustive. There are also smart books for extra credit.

He is very rude and condescending. I feel like he goes out of his way to make this class feel more important than it is. He reads from the slides most of the times. He takes attendance atleast once a week and be ready to read alot and do the smart books. I think this class especially with Dr.Faulk would be better with a different professor.
He's really funny in his lectures which are long but funny sometimes. Offers 15 extra credit points and has a very clear grading structure. If you learn the review sheet, you'll do well on the exams.

Dr. Faulk class is straightforward and clear. Takes attendance once a week. Three tests with clear review and no trick questions. Discussion posts, homework and smartbook activities. Go to class because he will discuss test questions and answers in the lectures.

This class is genuinely easy if you do the reviews for each exam and stay on top of your work. Tests are straightforward and do not try to trick you. Memorization is key and most of it is common sense. Easy class and he makes a lot of jokes about his personal relationships which I thought were unnecessary but funny. Smart books are extra credit.
This class is a waste of everyones time.
The content that we are tested over is completely made up.

Professor Faulk's class was very easy. He takes attendance once a week on a random day. I would do the smartbook and homework assignments during the lecture. I got an A on every exam, and I just studied the lecture slides the week before the exam.

This class is literally a breeze. The exams are questions from the smartbooks, and the SB is extra credit; you can earn up to 15 points of extra credit. He takes attendance once a week, but doesn't say what day.

If you do the weekly smartbooks/homework/packbacks (you can complete in an hour each week) then the only thing that you're actually graded on is exams(3 exams). Exams are closed-note and only based on the notes, so you can get away with studying the day before the exam and still get a good grade. Take good notes from powerpoints and you're good.

Attendance is taken at random once per week. A lot of homework, but it is very easy. If you do the smartbook recharges (HW) and exam review before exams, you will get an A. He is a good lecturer and tells good stories, but the subject itself is quite boring.

Faulk really just read off the slides and went on random tangents about his past working at Dillards. He has a mix of HW assignments, packbacks, smartbooks and then his exams which contribute to most of the grade. Least favorite part about him was that half of his assignments are due at 6:00pm which in unbelievably inconvenient to most people.
This is a made up class that Mays needs to get rid of. Larry can go back to working at Dillards where he belongs.
The fact that he receives a salary from Texas A&M just proves that you can get paid to do anything.

Faulk was not my favorite professor. His teaching style is soooooooooo boring. Theres quite a bit of homework and the exams arent hard but definitely a class you cannot slack on. 3 exams, smartbooks, packbacks. Probably the lest engaging professor ive ever met. I always wanted to fall asleep in his class.
Just make quiz lets over the exam reviews and do the smart books and you'll get an A on every exam. Then just show up for the attendance grades and do the extra credit and you'll get a B minimum.

There is attendance once a week and you don't know which day it is. To be honest you won't learn much of anything in class besides his personal experiences. You can genuinely learn the material just by memorizing the review. You will have to study for the tests just because there's a lot of material. Not a bad class just don't neglect it.

Professor Faulk delivers engaging lectures, and the exams are straightforward if you understand the material and can apply it to the situations given to you. He also takes attendance once a week, so make sure to attend class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework, packbacks, and graded attendance. The lectures are pretty boring. Some extra credit.

This professor doesn't care about his students. I had a 79 and he left it as a C and did not round up. He reads straight off the slides and I feel like I was teaching myself. People only go to class when he takes attendance and class is so TEST HEAVY. The test reviews are not like the exams. Good luck he's the only professor for 363!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Required attendance once a week randomly. However, recommend you go to every class cause things he says stuff in class that shows up on exams. Exams aren't meant to trick you & are straightforward. Offers good extra credit. Do the smart book and exam review before each exam and you will be fine. He goes on tangents in class which can get boring...
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Eternal lectures but easy class and a very nice guy. Used online textbook to get through everything, he takes attendance at random once a week. Exams are straightforward but can get quite specific.

Go to class even if you get your attendance for the week. He covers things not in the textbook that WILL be on the exams. Exam grades matter so don't slack and genuinely study the review guide. dont rely on common sense, genuinely understand it. you need to read the textbook and review slides, and do the smartbook/hw to do well. Use quizlets!!

Class is fairly easy but the lectures are just so boring its miserable to sit through. He takes attendance once a week at random, or on guest speaker days. So u can skip class after he takes it. Anywhere from 2-3 assignments(including a packback) a week but theyre not difficult. Def do the extra credit even if it takes awhile, its not hard.
Boring class, lots to memorize. But exams are straightforward.

Not that hard of a class, I usually didn't study till the day before the exams because they all lined up with FINC341, so I didn't do great. Professor Faulk is pretty good; he goes off on tangents, but is honestly really entertaining and uses funny examples. He does random attendance days, so I never skipped class.

There I am, sitting quietly in the front row of the lecture (for the extra legroom). As I begin to zone out, a loud "That's right!" shakes the room. My eyes trail upwards as I see Professor Faulk pacing back and forth with a sly smile on his face. He pauses for but a moment, creating suspense and intrigue, then proclaims

"Hunter Biden's Laptop!"

class is extremely easy, and unfortunately you have to take it.

mandatory attendance one random day a week.

Larry is extremely slow and goes on personal tangents, super political, just show up everyday until he takes attendance, then skip for the rest of the week and take notes off the powerpoints. If you turn something in late it is a 0!

I think Professor Faulk did a good job at teaching this class. Sometimes I found it hard to pay attention because he mainly just reads off the slides, but tests are very straightforward and he provides a study guide. There is also extra credit built into the class which is nice.

Class is generally common sense, but largely due to his personality I don't recommend taking this professor. Frequently goes on tangents that vaguely connect to course material, often trying to force his own political views upon course concepts. Attendance is mandatory once a week.

He is a great professor! The concepts are pretty easy too. He takes attendance one day a week so be sure to go to class! There is a bit of homework, but they don't weigh that much. There are three exams (multiple choice) - they weigh a ton.
this class feels like common sense. i only go because he takes attendance on one random day of the week.

Prof Faulk is a charismatic teacher who is engaging and gives you what you need to succeed. He will make you laugh and the content is interesting if you remotely care about the topics. Attendance is mandatory he takes attendance once a week only. The reviews have everything you need for exams so just memorize all of that and attend class.

Attendance is part of ur grade. He does not allow you to see ur grade in canvas so u have to calculate on ur own. Lectures are boring but he's a really nice and sweet professor. I do feel bad sometimes because the content is mundane but don't think it's his fault, I wouldn't know how you can make this course interesting. It's just one of those.

I didn't personally like this professor but this class is not hard. Just learn whats on the test reviews and have it memorized because the answer choices will be similar and a slight change in words can mess you up. Do the extra credit its worth it. If theres no attendance no need to show up to class its pointless.

I was decimals away from an A (did everything to best of my abilities til finals forgot a hw) and he basically said too bad - no matter how stressed you are in life do not let it in your way with this class because it might cost u everything. he does not let you see your grade until the moment he finalize it, and people only show up for attendance.

He takes attendance once a week (you don't know on what day), but other than that there is no point in showing up to class. He reads directly off the slides that are posted on Canvas. The tests are super easy its just a lot of information to memorize. Easy A if you study and do the homework.

Lectures are simply him reading from the textbook, but you have to go because attendance is worth points. He frequently rambles about random things and lectures are terrible and a massive waste of time. Exams are always harder than you think, but he does give you a review guide. Take someone else if you can.

Good professor, boring class. The most annoying part was that every exam fell on the same day as the ACCT 327 exams. You def need to study a good amount bc it's straight definitions/smartbook. I would just redo SB and do some quizlets and score fine. The first test was easy, the 2nd/3rd were the same difficulty but a little harder.

Professor Faulk is very nice and understanding. I enjoyed the guest speakers but the lectures can difficult to be engaged in. My biggest mistake was putting off the homework and forgetting it as it can be due at different times such as noon or 6pm. If you do all the assignments and do the study guide, an A is obtainable.

Would take attendance once a week but other than that he was a really chill professor and even offered extra credit! Exams were exactly like the reviews and came from lectures and powerpoints! Such a chill class tbh and an easy A if you study the review and complete the assignments also gave extra credit to those that came to class b4 spring break

Lectures were mostly engaging, covering the material and what was needed for the test. Going to class every day was good for catching little questions on tests that the book didn't cover completely. I enjoyed going to class and didn't have a problem with the tests. Do the smartbooks for extra credit and stay on top of homework due dates.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: if you put in the work an a is easy to achieve, tests are super important. don't miss an attendance day and DO SMARTBOOKS they will add like 10 points to your grade. he's caring but man are his lectures a drag. he does his best to make them engaging but if you don't like sports it's a rough time. only prof offered right now

such a great guy, knows how to lecture and is very knowledgable about the concepts. I wish he taught more courses here... I would take all of them even if I did not have to. Show up to class, pay attention and you will be fine. I still made flashcards though. Provided study guides for exams.

Average class and teacher, overall boring class but he makes it tolerable, just do homework and make sure to not skip class because he does attendance once a week. Also do homeworks because if you dont it adds up real fast

Attendance is a part of the grade so make sure you don't skip class. The content itself is very simple and mostly common sense. Although his lectures are pretty boring, Professor Faulk does offer extra credit and only takes attendance once a week.

Show up to class (attendance matters), do the HW and extra credit. Study the notes taken in class (write down as much as you can), then do the extra credit smartbooks again once or twice. Go to exams, take exams, go home. That's basically this class. Otherwise, he is boring and goes off track a lot
He's nice, but wants to make his grade distribution lower.

Not a hard class at all, but make sure you never miss a day of attendance. I ended with an 89.7 in this class, which he didn't round up. You want to make sure you have plenty of cushion, because he does not curve or round.

Professor Faulk's lectures can be somewhat boring and not many people show up unless there is a guest speaker (attendance is still semi-mandatory though). He does provide exam review docs which can help out greatly when figuring out what to expect on the exams. HW/extra credit is pretty easy since it's done through McGraw-Hill.

Mr. Faulk is the sweetest ever. I'm so sad about the negative reviews. His class may be a little boring, but I enjoyed the guest speakers. He is super friendly and kind and will answer any questions. His class was a breeze and a nice break from all the rigor of other classes in Mays. He only takes attendance once a week and offers extra credit!

One of the most boring classes I've ever taken, the professor is nice but he promotes no critical thinking. The exams are strictly memorization of the 200+ terms in the book. Would never take this class if not forced too. stay safe yall.
Definitely take your own notes from the textbook and redo the SmartBooks until you mastered the concepts. This class is easy and Faulk is a good, caring professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's honestly a funny guy. He explains the material well and asks for the "muddiest point" everyday when class ends. 2nd exam is weirdly harder than the first so be prepared for that. He took attendance once a week. Material is not that hard, but invest in Quizlet Plus & make your own flashcards each week for each chapter and you'll be fine!

Prof. Faulk isn't necessarily the most engaging prof, but he communicated about mgmt well and likes sport and movie references. About 1/2 the class doesn't sit in lecture past the 1st week as the concepts are covered in the book. Connect h/w for each ch, and extra credit for 'smart book' completion. Easy A if you make sure to do his review guides!
Grade is mostly based on three tests throughout the semester so make sure you are prepared because if you mess up on the first one it is really difficult to recover.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not underestimate this class!! His lectures are incredibly boring - make sure to carefully read the textbook and take notes. When it comes to studying for the test, you are basically expected to memorize the textbook - the tests are very specific. If you make 363 a priority an A is doable, but Larry Faulk is not one of my favorite professors.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'd rather kick rocks than learn this boring material. The professor is ok, but nothing great. Only has 3 tests and short hw assignments from McGraw Hill over each chapter. Gives a few extra bonus points for doing smart book questions. He's the only professor offered for this class during the year at the moment so good luck.

This is one of the most boring classes I have taken at Mays and the test are entirely too complicated compared to the simplicity of the homework material. This is not a very difficult class but do not underestimate the tests as one bad test grade seriously sets you back. All said, Larry Faulk is not a good professor, take someone else.

Dr. Faulk is a super chill prof. His class is super easy and is only graded by 3 exams (90%) and HWs (10%). The study guides he provide have everything you need to know for the exam. Read the smartbooks too. This class is comparable (difficulty-wise) to ISTM 210.

Larry did a good job of keeping this class entertaining and I genuinely learned. If you pay attention during lecture and take notes, it will save you SO much time when you start studying for the exam. Honestly if you start filling out the review during/after lecture you should be good. The hw is super easy and do the smartbooks for extra credit.
Class is very boring but if you go and at least listen a little you only have to study max 1 hour before the test.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very average prof. 363 is very vocab heavy, lectures are a snooze-fest but you don't have to go if you're fine cramming 200 terms before an exam.

Not really a need to go to lectures, the material is simply ALOT (150-200 for each exam) of straight-forward, non-complex terms and definitions you need to memorize for the tests. Smartbook extra credit is a lot of work for insignificant extra credit. Discussion sessions really eat at your grade if you get a tough TA. Locks canvas grade so annoying

Very nice guy but classes are incredibly dry. Content is extremely mundane and mostly textbook material, however, the tests are specific and difficult comparatively. Homework is easy, just make sure you're doing the right one because the chapters don't advance chronologically. Overall, the prof does his best but this class lacks substance.
Class is straightforward. Pretty much impossible to get a C. Lot of information however that needs to be memorized. The breakout classes can be annoying but sometimes they were fun. Nice guy.

Professor Faulk is a sweetheart and is very intelligent! Although, this class is lots of material to remember and exams are worth your whole grade. He usually puts up reviews for exams but you need to study for hours to remember every single detail. Faulk is a great professor but the class structure needs help.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Faulk is one of those dry professors. He lectures and covers the material, but it is also the most excruciatingly boring thing to sit through. He's a nice guy, but not very understanding on any extenuating circumstances. I think this class is an easy B class, but definitely not an easy A. His tests count for a lot!

Probably one of the worst professors I have had at Mays. Half the class does not even go since there is no point, because you won't learn anything from the lectures I was also told I had bad time management skills when asked for an extension on the exam. You need to know the textbook front and back to be successful in his class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were good, I was always entertained cause he told a lot of stories. This class was just tough for me because there were 3 exams and they accounted for over 80% of the overall grade. He has exam reviews and I did them before every exam but when the exam was in front of me there were multiple things the review did not cover.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy CBK class and the assignments are not difficult. I stopped going to lectures after the first test because he posted reviews that were identical to his tests. Attendance is required on Fridays for discussion sessions but you just have to talk enough about an article and you're fine. My TA was nice with grading, but I also put in effort.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was fairly easy, I stopped going to lectures cause he posts the powerpoint and exams are pretty much that. If you do exam reviews you'll be fine for the exams. Big thing is discussion group, you just have to get lucky with your TA. Mine was chill and gave out 8s even if we didn't say much but I know others who would got 5/6 for same thing
Professor Faulk is a good professor. I eventually stopped going to class because I didn't find the lectures very useful, but he's a nice guy and it's not too hard to make a good grade in this class.

Faulk is such a sweetheart! Like I want to be his friend lol. He posts all the slides online (as well as a synopsis of the whole textbook basically), so I stopped going to class after the first exam; saw very little change in my exam grades thereafter. Friday discussion sessions are annoying; you def won't get all 10 points each week (I never did)

Lectures are extremely boring, your discussion participation matters so make sure you do good for that. Tests cover a lot of material and he grabs the nitty gritty details from the notes. No need to go to class at all.

had an A in the class which dropped to a C after the last two exams, definitely did not like the three exam structure in this class. the second exam had a ridiculous amount of material to memorize which ultimately cost me my A... be ready to use Quizlet for this class

The two worst parts were discussion sessions and dry lectures. The easiest parts were the SmartBook extra credit assignments and the tests that are majorly outlined by his test reviews. This class is an easy A as long as you can read a chapter a week and say 2-3 things during each discussion session; it doesn't have to be ground-breaking either.

Prof. Faulk's teaching method was not the best nor the worst. He gave great real life examples of the concepts, but his lectures were overall pretty dry. There is not a large margin of error with your grade because the tests account for 450/550 total points. Do the exam reviews and re-read the lecture guides and you will be fine.

Faulk is very chill and he does he best to make lectures entertaining, but they still can be dry. Study the chapter summaries that he posts before the exams and you should be fine. The TA sessions are annoying, because you will get a 7 or 8 no matter what and it drags your grade down. This class is an easy B, but to get an A will take some effort.

Professor Faulk is great professor and his lectures were really interesting until I stopped going because they weren't needed to perform well on exams. The structure with discussion sections and harshly the TA decides the grade them is the reason I pulled a B rather than an A because I only got 8's and 9's and never a 10. Good prof, bad structuring

Just do the study guide based off of notes you take from the textbook. No need to go to class if you've taken good notes that answer the study guide well. Know that there are only three tests including the final so one bad test grade could make or break your chances of getting an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice and caring professor. He gives real world examples in his lectures but they usually don't matter for the test. You really just need to make sure you show up for the discussion labs and you will be good. Make sure to read/do the study guide and you're golden! Tests are really easy and he will drop lowest homework/quiz grade.
